socfpga_ecc.h

ECC hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

The ECC driver provides a low-level interface to manage Error Correction Code controllers across the SoCFPGA HPS. It handles the enable/disable sequences, fault injection (for both MMIO-based and SiP-managed blocks), and interrupt tracking for SBE (Single-Bit Error) and DBE (Double-Bit Error) events.

Types
socfpga_ecc_block_t

Identifiers for every ECC-protected memory block within the HPS subsystem.

Values
SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_NONE

No block selected.

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_OCRAM

On-chip RAM ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_USB0_RAM0

USB0 RAM0 ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_USB1_RAM2

USB1 RAM2 ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC0_RX

EMAC0 RX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC0_TX

EMAC0 TX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC1_RX

EMAC1 RX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC1_TX

EMAC1 TX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC2_RX

EMAC2 RX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_EMAC2_TX

EMAC2 TX buffer ECC block (MMIO).

SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_USB1_RAM1

Defines the classification of the ECC fault detected by the controller.

socfpga_ecc_init
int32_t socfpga_ecc_init(
void
)

Initializes the ECC driver context. This routine resolves the base addresses for all peripheral blocks, masks the global System Manager ECC interrupts (to prevent spurious triggers during init), and registers the SERR/DERR ISRs with the GIC.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code if the initialization fails (e.g., duplicate init).

socfpga_ecc_deinit
int32_t socfpga_ecc_deinit(
void
)

Deinitializes the ECC driver. This masks all ECC interrupts in the System Manager and clears the registered user callback.

Returns

0 on success; negative on error.

socfpga_ecc_enable_blocks
int32_t socfpga_ecc_enable_blocks(
uint32_t 
block_mask
)

Enables ECC checking and correction for the specified blocks.

This performs a safe enable sequence: disabling interrupts, resetting the ECC engine and its associated memory, enabling detection/correction logic, and unmasking the SERR lines in the System Manager.

Parameters
block_mask
uint32_t

Bitmask of blocks to enable (using `1U << SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_...`).

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the mask is invalid; -EIO if hardware fails to acknowledge reset.

socfpga_ecc_disable_blocks
int32_t socfpga_ecc_disable_blocks(
uint32_t 
block_mask
)

Disables ECC checking and correction for the specified blocks.

Parameters
block_mask
uint32_t

Bitmask of blocks to disable.

Returns

0 on success; negative on error.

socfpga_ecc_inject_block_err
int32_t socfpga_ecc_inject_block_err(
uint32_t 
block,
uint32_t 
err_type
)

Injects a synthetic ECC error into an MMIO-accessible HPS block for validation testing. This writes to the per-block `ECC_INT_TEST` register.

Parameters
block
uint32_t

The target socfpga_ecc_block_t ID.

err_type
uint32_t

The error type to inject (<SOCFPGA_ECC_ERR_SBE> or <SOCFPGA_ECC_ERR_DBE>).

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the block is unsupported or invalid.

socfpga_ecc_inject_ddr_err
int32_t socfpga_ecc_inject_ddr_err(
uint32_t 
syndrome,
uint32_t 
command
)

Triggers a synthetic ECC error in DDR memory via the IO96B controller.  This issues an `INTEL_SIP_SMC_INJECT_IO96B_ECC_ERR` call to the Secure Monitor (ATF), which handles the interaction with the IO96B controller.

Parameters
syndrome
uint32_t

The syndrome value encoding bit positions for the synthetic error.

command
uint32_t

The specific trigger/control op-code as defined by the SiP documentation.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code if the SiP call fails.

socfpga_ecc_get_hw_sbe_count
int32_t socfpga_ecc_get_hw_sbe_count(
uint32_t 
block
)

Reads the hardware-accumulated SBE counter (ECC_S_ERR_CNT) directly from the memory controller of the specified block. This is useful for polling status if interrupts are not available.

Parameters
block
uint32_t

The block ID.

Returns

The current hardware counter value; -EINVAL on invalid or disabled block.

socfpga_ecc_poll_status
int32_t socfpga_ecc_poll_status(
uint32_t 
*
out_serr_bits,
uint32_t 
*
out_derr_bits
)

Manually polls the System Manager SERR/DERR status bits. This is primarily intended for diagnostic CLI commands or systems where GIC interrupts are not available.

This function clears the status bits (Write-1-to-Clear) and updates the software counters. Note: User callbacks are NOT invoked during this polling cycle as it operates in a non-interrupt context.

Parameters
out_serr_bits
uint32_t*

Pointer to receive the raw SERR status word handled during the poll.

out_derr_bits
uint32_t*

Pointer to receive the raw DERR status word handled during the poll.

Returns

The number of total events handled (count of set bits cleared).

socfpga_ecc_clear_counters
int32_t socfpga_ecc_clear_counters(
uint32_t 
block
)

Resets the software-tracked SBE and DBE counters for a specific block to zero.

Parameters
block
uint32_t

The block ID, or SOCFPGA_ECC_BLOCK_NONE to clear all blocks.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the block ID is invalid.

socfpga_ecc_set_callback
int32_t socfpga_ecc_set_callback(
socfpga_ecc_callback_t 
callback
)

Registers a user-defined ISR callback function. This will be invoked by the internal ISR after the driver has finished processing a block's SBE/DBE event.

Parameters
callback
socfpga_ecc_callback_t

Function pointer to the ISR handler; pass NULL to unregister.

Returns

0 on success.
